toor_dal.note: Cooks faster; slightly softer, sweeter than toor.
Milder and lighter; reduce cooking time.
Nuttier and firmer; soak first and cook longer.

masoor_dal.note: Both cook quickly; moong is a touch milder.
Earthier; needs a little longer to soften.

chana_dal.note: Softer and quicker; loses the firm bite of chana.
Milder and softer; works in tempering, not for crunch.

urad_dal.note: For vada/batter body only; lacks urad's binding stickiness.

whole_moong.note: Split cooks much faster; skip the sprouting step.

kabuli_chana.note: Nuttier, firmer, darker gravy; soak overnight.

black_chana.note: Softer and lighter; milder earthy flavour.

rajma.note: Different texture but holds up in thick gravies.

green_peas_dried.note: Fresh/frozen peas skip soaking; add near the end.

green_peas.note: Soak and boil dried peas before use.

cooking_oil.note: Adds a coastal aroma; ideal for Kerala/Konkan dishes.
Nutty gingelly note; classic for pickles and Chettinad.
Pungent; heat to smoking first to mellow it.
Richer flavour; lower smoke point, avoid deep-frying.
For sauteing only; burns easily, watch the heat.

mustard_oil.note: Neutral; misses the sharp pungency of mustard oil.

sesame_oil.note: Neutral; add a few sesame seeds for aroma.
Regional swap in South Indian cooking.

ghee.note: Use unsalted; clarify by skimming for a closer match.
Loses the nutty richness; fine for everyday cooking.

butter.note: Use a bit less; ghee is pure fat with no water.

green_chili.note: Deeper, smokier heat; less fresh sharpness.
Add to taste; no fresh bite, adjust for colour too.
Only for bulk/colour when heat is not wanted; no pungency.

dried_red_chili.note: Roughly 1 chili to 1/2 tsp powder; add during tempering carefully.
Brighter, fresher heat; add later in cooking.

red_chili_powder.note: Milder with more colour; increase quantity for same heat.
Grind or use whole; adjust quantity to taste.

kashmiri_chili_powder.note: Hotter and less vivid; use less to keep heat in check.

tamarind.note: Brighter sourness; add at the end off the heat.
Use about 1 tsp per lime-sized tamarind; no liquid added.
Fruity tang; common in coastal gravies.
Seasonal souring; adds body and pulp.

lemon.note: Deeper, earthier sour; dissolve pulp in water first.
Dry tang without liquid; add a pinch at a time.

amchur.note: Use a squeeze in place of a pinch; adds moisture.
Wetter and darker; dissolve and reduce.

kokum.note: Similar tang; use pulp, adjust to taste.
Seasonal fruity souring for coastal curries.

coconut.note: Ready grated; roughly one cup per half a fresh coconut.
Reconstitute or roast; more concentrated, less moisture.

grated_coconut.note: Grate fresh coconut just before use.
Soak or use as is for chutney; slightly chewy.
For gravies only; adds liquid, not texture.

dry_coconut.note: Fresh is moister; roast lightly to mimic copra depth.
Grate fresh; use a bit more for the same richness.

coconut_milk.note: Grind grated coconut with warm water and strain.
Last resort; loses coconut flavour, thin the gravy less.
For richness only; no coconut note, use diluted.

jaggery.note: Use slightly less; lacks the caramel, mineral depth.
Darker and deeper; near one-to-one swap.

palm_jaggery.note: Milder cane flavour; near one-to-one swap.
Cleaner sweetness; misses the smoky palm note.

sugar.note: Adds colour and depth; use a little more, dissolve well.
Add off the heat; increases moisture, reduce other liquid.

curd.note: For gravies; add a souring agent to mimic tang, do not boil hard.
Richer, non-tangy; good for kormas, add lemon for tartness.

milk.note: Vegan; adds coconut flavour, use thin milk.
Whisk with water to loosen; adds tang.

cream.note: Thinner; simmer to reduce or add a little cashew paste.
Whisk well and add off heat to avoid splitting.

paneer.note: Only for crumbled fillings/sweets, not for cubes.

khoa.note: For sweets; much sweeter, cut the added sugar.
Crumble and cook down with a little milk and sugar.

rice_flour.note: For crispness/binding; corn flour is more starchy.

corn_flour.note: For coating crispness; less thickening power in sauces.
Thickens gravies; makes them cloudier, cook longer.

maida.note: Denser, browner result; fine for rotis and thickening.

wheat_flour.note: Lighter and less nutritious; adjust water in doughs.

rava.note: For batters only; grind poha, texture differs.

poha.note: Lighter and crispier; loses poha's soft body.

sambar_powder.note: Rough swap; rasam powder is more peppery, add coriander and chili.

rasam_powder.note: Rough swap; sambar powder is milder, add extra pepper and cumin.

coriander_leaves.note: Stronger, cooler flavour; use less as a garnish.

mint_leaves.note: Milder; loses the cooling menthol note.

fenugreek_leaves.note: Use about a third the amount; crush and add near the end.
For bulk greens only; add a pinch of fenugreek seeds for bitterness.

kasuri_methi.note: Use roughly three times the amount of fresh leaves.

spinach.note: Adds bitterness; blanch and use less.

shallots.note: Use regular onion chopped fine; less sweet and intense.

onion.note: Sweeter and more aromatic; use more by weight.

ginger_garlic_paste.note: Combine with garlic; grind fresh in equal parts.
Combine with ginger; grind fresh in equal parts.

ginger.note: Use about a quarter tsp powder per inch of fresh; no moisture.

dry_ginger.note: Use grated fresh ginger; add more, it is milder.

cashew.note: Blanch and grind for a pale, rich gravy paste.
Roast and skin; nuttier, good in chutneys and pastes.
For white gravy thickening; soak and grind.

peanut.note: Creamier, milder; good in chutneys and pastes.
For chutney body; toast first, more bitter.

sesame_seeds.note: For thickening gravies; poppy is milder, soak first.
For chutney bulk; roast, coarser texture.

poppy_seeds.note: For gravy thickening/whiteness; richer, use less.

bottle_gourd.note: Similar mild gourd; peel ridges, cooks a bit faster.
Comparable watery texture in kootu and curries.
Milder and softer; good in dals and stews.

ridge_gourd.note: Milder; use in the same curries.

snake_gourd.note: Milder, firmer; works in the same dishes.

potato.note: Holds shape well in curries; par-boil, less starchy.
Similar starchy bite; par-boil to reduce stickiness.
Adds sweetness; use where a sweet note is acceptable.

raw_banana.note: Softer and starchier; reduce cooking time.
Similar firm texture in dry curries.

colocasia.note: Less sticky; par-boil for a similar bite.
Firmer tuber; comparable in masala fries.

cluster_beans.note: French beans are less bitter; cook a little less.

chicken.note: Vegetarian swap in masala gravies; add later, do not overcook.
Meaty vegetarian option; releases water, saute first.

prawns.note: Use firm fish chunks; adjust cooking time to avoid breaking.

vinegar.note: Milder and fruitier; use more, add off the heat.
